newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight ends at 5.5 pct on bank lending.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight ends at 5.5 pct on bank lending.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate closed at 5.5 percent on aggressive lending by foreign banks long on ringgit, dealers said on Wednesday.
The lending started late in the day after the overnight had earlier stabilised around 6.5/7.0 percent after opening at 8.0 percent, they said.
"It was quite sudden and the banks were lending all the way down from 7.0 percent. It was last taken at 5.5 percent," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
"Foreign banks were long on ringgit and had little choice but to offer back to the market due to the curbs on swaps transactions," he said.
Bank Negara announced on Sunday that local banks would have to limit their non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer, from Monday.
It said the move was to help control interest rates more effectively. The central bank has in the last two weeks been trying to lower interest rates in an effort to boost domestic economic activity.
Dealers said the overnight rate also fell ahead of the return of some funds at the end of the week.
There will be a maturity of Bank Negara bills worth one billion ringgit on Friday.
